_disclaimer: DIRECTIONAL/ILLUSTRATIVE ONLY. Built from public secondary sources (state DOI sites, legal trackers, NAIC materials) during a design session, not from the actual filed rate manuals. Every record below is a starting skeleton showing HOW the registry should differ state-to-state - not a production-ready compliance source. Before this feeds a live rating decision: (1) pull the actual current filed rate manual/rules for each state and program, (2) re-verify every prohibited/permitted variable against current statute text, (3) get sign-off from whoever holds compliance/regulatory responsibility for the business.

states.regulator_name: New York Department of Financial Services

credit_based_insurance_score.notes: NY does not ban credit-based scoring outright, but any model using it falls under DFS AI/algorithmic oversight (see ai_governance) - verify current permitted-use scope.

ai_governance.citation: NY DFS Circular Letter 2024-7 requires insurers to demonstrate AI/external data systems do not proxy for protected classes, maintain explanatory documentation, allow DFS to review vendor tools, and require vendor audits. This is the strictest documentation bar of any state researched so far - build the decision-log/explainability feature to NY's standard by default so every other state is a subset, not a special case.

Required for MI PIP rating accuracy when the applicant has Medicare - affects the coordination-of-benefits rate factor.
Optional PIP add-on affecting premium; not required to submit but must be captured if selected.
